belief: “Other people are the reason I use. If they treated me better, I wouldn’t need it.”
belief_plain: Other people are the reason I use. If they treated me better, I wouldn’t need it
origins: Other people really can be part of the story. Stress, cruelty, loneliness, a house that was never safe, a loss someone else caused: those things hurt, and using may have been how you got through them. The lie goes one step further. It says you have no next step until they treat you better, and that the using is simply their fault. Their harm can be real and still not be the only thing that gets to decide your tomorrow. You can grieve what they did and still reach for help. You do not have to pretend you caused their treatment in order to get care for yourself. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure.
self: If they were kinder, I would not use.
This is on them, so I do not have to look at it.
Nothing will change until they change.
Getting help means I am letting them off the hook.
I am only doing what they drove me to.
replacement: People have hurt me, and that is real. Their treatment does not remove my next step. I can get help even if they do not change.
